consolidated_structures.name: Stating Factual Descriptions and Natural Functions in Present Simple (CLIL Science)
consolidated_structures.plain_english_explanation: Use the present simple with third-person subjects to state factual properties, operations, or habitats of things and animals in content-area lessons.

consolidated_structures.name: Asking and Answering About Actions in Progress (Present Continuous)
consolidated_structures.plain_english_explanation: Use 'What's he/she doing?' or 'What are they doing?' to ask about ongoing activities, answering with contracted pronouns and -ing verbs.

consolidated_structures.name: Expressing Classroom Directives and Rules (Imperatives)
consolidated_structures.plain_english_explanation: Give instructions using base verbs directly, or prohibit actions using 'Don't' followed by the base verb.

consolidated_structures.name: Asking and Stating Quantities with Existential There is / There are
consolidated_structures.plain_english_explanation: Ask about counts with 'How many [nouns] are there?' and answer with 'There's [one]' or 'There are [number]'.

consolidated_structures.name: Asking and Stating Daily Routine Times and Schedules
consolidated_structures.plain_english_explanation: Ask when routines and events happen using 'When do/does...', answering with the action verb and 'at [time]'.

consolidated_structures.name: Forming Wh- Information Questions with Be and Do
consolidated_structures.plain_english_explanation: Form open questions by pairing a Wh- word (Who, What, Where, When, How, How many) with the appropriate auxiliary or linking verb before the subject.

consolidated_structures.name: Asking and Stating Physical Abilities with Modal Can and Can't
consolidated_structures.plain_english_explanation: Ask whether someone or an animal has an ability using 'Can [subject] [base verb]?', answer with short forms ('Yes, it can' / 'No, they can't'), and state abilities directly with can/can't.

consolidated_structures.name: Prenominal Adjective Ordering Before Nouns
consolidated_structures.plain_english_explanation: Place multiple descriptive words in front of a noun following the order: opinion, size/shape, age, and color.

consolidated_foundational_skills.name: Subject Pronoun + Present 'Be' Contraction Recognition and Formation (He's, She's, It's, They're)
consolidated_foundational_skills.plain_english_explanation: Recognize, read, and write contracted forms of third-person subject pronouns with the present tense of 'be' (is -> 's, are -> 're).

related_knowledge.description: Aspectual contrast between actions happening right now and habitual or permanent facts.
related_knowledge.relationship: Unit 1 focuses exclusively on temporary actions currently in progress using Present Continuous (-ing), whereas Unit 6 and Unit 8 express recurring daily habits and permanent natural/scientific facts using Present Simple.

related_knowledge.description: Syntactic question formation across different verb categories (Be, Do, Modal Can).
related_knowledge.relationship: Inversion and auxiliary placement vary systematically by verb type: inverted 'be' in Unit 1 and Unit 6 ('What is she doing?', 'Who are you?'), auxiliary do-support in Unit 6 ('Where do you work?', 'When does he get up?'), and fronted modal auxiliary in Unit 8 ('Can a kangaroo jump?').

related_knowledge.description: Contraction mechanics: Pronoun + 'Be' affirmative contractions versus Modal negative contraction.
related_knowledge.relationship: Unit 1 and Unit 6 reinforce affirmative pronoun-verb contractions (he's, she's, it's, they're), while Unit 8 introduces the negative modal contraction 'can't' (cannot -> can't) with invariable modal syntax.

related_knowledge.description: Grammatical number concord across pronouns, existentials, and verbs.
related_knowledge.relationship: Singular versus plural distinctions require different mechanical rules across units: pronoun selection (he/she vs. they in Unit 1; it vs. they in Unit 8), existential selection (There's vs. There are in Unit 1), present simple inflection/auxiliary selection (base vs. -s/-es and do vs. does in Unit 6), contrasting with modal invariability (can/can't remains unchanged for singular and plural in Unit 8).

related_knowledge.description: Systematic phonics coverage of distinct consonant and vowel digraphs.
related_knowledge.relationship: Each unit includes dedicated phonics instruction targeting different sound-spelling correspondences: dental fricatives /θ/ and /ð/ (th) in Unit 1, affricates and palato-alveolar fricatives (ch, tch, sh) in Unit 6, and vowel digraphs /aʊ/ and /uː/ (ou, ow) in Unit 8.

related_knowledge.description: Recurring instructional task commands across textbook units.
related_knowledge.relationship: All three units share a consistent core of instructional command verbs directing student activity: 'listen', 'look', 'say', 'find', 'read', 'write', 'ask and answer', 'circle', 'match', and 'play a game'.

evidence_gaps.description: Units 2, 3, 4, 5, and 7 were not supplied in this experiment. Cross-unit transitions and intermediate reinforcement patterns between Unit 1, Unit 6, and Unit 8 cannot be determined without analyzing those intervening units.

Listening track dependencies noted in unit-level analyses (Unit 1 Tracks 15 and 21; Unit 6 Tracks 122 and 133; Unit 8 Tracks 167 and 177) prevent independent verification of specific audio answer keys across all three units.
